metadata.description: DeepSeek Harness 插件：任务执行到第 X 步起，每 Y 步往智能体自己的上下文里注入一次自定义消息（共 Z 次，文案支持 {{step}} 占位），并可在用户消息末尾追加一句话；带总开关，全部在设置页配置。Scheduled context injection for DSH agents.

# dsh-insert-context
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that inserts context into an agent **during** a task, on a schedule
you define. Three switches, all configured from DSH's Settings page:

0. **Master switch** (`enabled`, **on by default**) — when off the plugin is completely inert: no
ru

le message, no append, and the step counter stops too, so switching it back on resumes the
schedule

where it stopped instead of firing every rule the silent steps had already passed.
1. **Rule injecti

on** — a rule says *from step X, every Y steps, Z times, with this text*. When the
agent's current s

tep number is one of the steps the rule hits, the text is injected as one extra
context message. `{{

step}}` in the text is replaced by the current step number.
2. **Append to every user message** — on

e sentence is appended to the end of each user message you
send. **Off by default**; turn it on in S

ettings if you want it. A second switch,
**append to subagents** (`appendSubagents`, also off by def

ault), decides whether messages *sent
to subagents* (via `delegate` / `send_message`) get the append

too — they are tagged as user
messages just like yours, so without this switch they would be indist

inguishable. A third switch,
**append to the first message only** (`appendFirstOnly`, **on by defaul

t**), turns the append
into a one-shot: only the first user message of the conversation carries the

sentence, every
later user message is left untouched.

Either behaviour can be turned off (an empty rule list injects nothing; `userAppend: false` stops
th

e append — the shipped default), and nothing is injected unless a rule or the append is actually
con

— the shipped default), and nothing is injected unless a rule or the append is actually
configured.
## Rules
A rule is `{ start, every, repeat, text }`. Its **hit set** is

| `{ start: 10, every: 10, repeat: 0 }` | 10, 20, 30, 40, … forever (**unlimited**) |
| `{ start: 5,

`repeat: 0` is the special value for **unlimited**: from `start` onwards the rule fires on every
`ev

ery`-th step and never stops (`repeat` is validated as 0–1000, where 0 means unlimited). The
Setting

s page previews an unlimited rule as `将注入第 10,20,30,… 步（无限次）` — the preview lists the
first 10 hits
and never walks an endless list.

So free-form intervals are possible — inject on 5, 10, 15 … 50 and then on 60, 70 … 100 by listing
t
wo rules. Rules are independent: one agent can be hit by any number of them.

`{{step}}` is the **only** supported placeholder, and it is only recognised in a rule's `text`
(not

in `appendText`). It is replaced by the current step number of that agent's counter — the same
count

er described under *Step counting* below. Any other `{{…}}` is left in the text verbatim and
logged
as a warning by the host (prefix `insert-context:`), never silently swallowed:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Several rules on the same step

If one step hits several rules, they are **merged into a single injected message**: each hit rule
co

ntributes one paragraph with its own `{{step}}` filled in, and the paragraphs are joined with a
newl

ine in the order the rules appear in the settings list (`rules[0]` first). One hit — one
message, no

matter how many rules matched. Reordering the rows on the Settings page therefore
reorders the para

how many rules matched. Reordering the rows on the Settings page therefore
reorders the paragraphs.
### Step counting
The counter is **per agent**, keyed by the agent id of the step payload, and it is dropped when that
agent is disposed (`agent/disposed`). Steps that are rejected downstream are not counted, and neith

er
are steps taken while the master switch (`enabled`) is off — the counter simply freezes, so switc

hing
the plugin back on resumes the schedule where it stopped. There is
**no layer filtering**: a di

spatcher and each of its subagents keep separate counters, so a subagent
that is on its 5th step is

hit by `{ start: 5, every: 5, repeat: 9 }` even if its parent is on step
50. Counting starts from th
e moment the plugin is mounted/active.
### Duplicate suppression
If a step already appended the sentence to a user message (behaviour 2), no rule message is injected
for that same step — the appended sentence already ends the batch, and a second copy is noise.

## How it works

The plugin listens on the host event `agent/pre-step`. It awaits the downstream decision and, when
t

he step is admitted, rewrites the messages that step will carry. A switched-off plugin
(`enabled: fa

lse`) returns that decision untouched before doing anything else — no counter, no
append, no rule me

returns that decision untouched before doing anything else — no counter, no
append, no rule message:

- every message whose `source.kind === 'user'` gets one extra trailing `text` block when
`userAppend

` is on — the user's own text is never modified; the sentence is its own paragraph.
A subagent's pro

mpts also carry `source.kind === 'user'` (they are sent by the dispatcher), so
the plugin checks whi

ch agent the step belongs to: inside a subagent (delegation depth ≥ 1, or
session origin `subagent`)

the append is skipped unless `appendSubagents` is on;
- one standalone `user` message (source kind

`insert-context`) is appended when the step number
hits at least one rule, carrying the merged parag

t-context`) is appended when the step number
hits at least one rule, carrying the merged paragraphs.

Because the agent loop journals `decision.messages` into the session log as `user/message` events
(`

surfaceOp: "append"`), both are durable: they are part of the committed context, survive replay
and
are exactly what the model reads on that step.
